metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to search for drip coffee makers on Google Shopping but encountered SSL cert error (NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID). Navigated to Amazon instead, searched 'drip coffee maker', applied color/price/deals filters, scrolled results. Later tried Google Shopping URL but landed on Best Buy. Failed after 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome address bar, type URLs, search products on Amazon, use search filters (color, price, deals), scroll through results, interact with web elements
metadata.failure_analysis: Google Shopping inaccessible due to SSL certificate error. Model could not bypass the cert error and tried alternative shopping sites instead. Evaluator expected Google Shopping-specific URL and filter states.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original complex shopping task into a simple Chrome settings navigation task. Model demonstrated ability to type URLs in address bar throughout the trajectory, so navigating to chrome://settings is within capability and avoids SSL issues.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to Chrome's settings page (chrome://settings). Evaluator uses URL pattern matching to verify the active tab URL contains 'chrome://settings'. Uses official getter active_url_from_accessTree and metric is_expected_url_pattern_match.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction requires opening Chrome's settings page. Evaluator checks if active tab URL matches 'chrome://settings' pattern — this correctly and fully verifies the requirement.
Getter active_url_from_accessTree extracts the current URL from the accessibility tree address bar, which is the right state to check for navigation tasks.
Metric is_expected_url_pattern_match uses re.search to find the pattern 'chrome://settings' in the result URL, which correctly verifies the URL contains the settings path.
Metric parameter handling is correct: expected.type='rule' means the metric receives rules dict directly, and it accesses rules['expected'] which contains the pattern list.

Minor concern: getter prepends default goto_prefix='https://' to the address bar text, producing 'https://chrome://settings'. However, re.search (not fullmatch) finds 'chrome://settings' within this string, so verification still succeeds.
No postconfig needed — URL state is persistent and accessible without reopening any UI.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider setting goto_prefix to empty string in the getter config to avoid the spurious 'https://' prefix on chrome:// URLs, e.g. {"type": "active_url_from_accessTree", "goto_prefix": ""}. While the current setup works due to re.search, an exact match scenario would fail.
